news.title: How to watch New Zealand play for place at FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand play New Caledonia on Friday to decide which of the sides will qualify for next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup. They meet in the semi-finals of the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship in Samoa, after Solomon Islands and Tahiti contest the other semi-final. The finalists at the OFC tournament will represent Oceania at next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Both games will be streamed live and free by OFC Media via their YouTube channel.

Mexico City Former Barcelona star Rafael Márquez was introduced on Thursday as the new head coach of the Mexican national team, aiming to qualify the squad for the 2030 World Cup.

news.title: French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support
news.lede: ‘Image and unity’ of game affected, FFF president says. It will consult sacked former Fifa official Kevin Lamour. The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election. The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June.

news.title: FIFA denies claim that Morocco will host 2030 World Cup final
news.lede: FIFA previously denied reports in the British media that its embattled president, Gianni Infantino, had promised Morocco the final in exchange for political support. ZURICH – FIFA has responded to a claim by the president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation that his nation would host the 2030 World Cup final, saying that decision has not been made yet. Morocco will co-host the 2030 tournament with Spain and Portugal. It marks just the second time an African nation will host World Cup games, after South Africa staged the 2010 event.

news.title: Japan end Bangladesh’s unbeaten run, World Cup dream
news.lede: Bangladesh’s hopes of securing a place in the FIH Women’s Junior World Cup were dashed on Thursday as the women in red and green suffered a 2-0 defeat to Japan in the quarterfinals of the Women’s Junior Asia Cup in China. Bangladesh will now play a fifth-sixth place-deciding match against either Malaysia or South Korea. The top four teams in the tournament will qualify for the next edition of the Women’s Junior World Cup. The women in red and green entered the quarterfinals as unbeaten champions of the Challenger Pool, having won all four of their matches.

news.title: Nigeria to hold legends match honoring football generation of the 1990s
news.lede: A football legends match dedicated to the generation of Nigerian players from the mid-1990s will take place on November 8 at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena in Lagos, Nigeria. The initiative was announced by the African Export-Import Bank, Afreximbank, through its Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) programme and TopTier Sports Management, Premium Times Nigeria reports. The match will be part of the CANEX WKND 2026 programme. According to the organizers, football stars from Nigeria, other African countries and beyond are expected to take part.
